notes: Deterministic, network-free vectors for the ID-Token *profile* rules that make an ID Token an ID Token — the checks layered on top of standard JWT validation (signature/iss/aud/iat/exp, covered by validation.json). Each vector supplies the already-decoded `input.claims`, the ID-Token JOSE-header `input.header_alg`, and the caller inputs (`client_id`, the `trusted_audiences` list of additional audiences the client trusts — absent means none — the opt-in `validate_azp` switch — absent means false — the opt-in `nonce`/`access_token`/`code`/`max_age`/`leeway`, and the `access_token_issued_with_id_token`/`code_issued_with_id_token` switches — absent means true), plus a fixed `input.now` (POSIX seconds) so `auth_time`/`max_age` freshness is clock-independent. Vectors are LANGUAGE-NEUTRAL: an `accept` outcome means every profile rule passes; a `reject` outcome carries a canonical `error` family (`id_token_profile`) plus a stable `reason` label (one of: missing_sub, missing_aud, untrusted_audience, azp_required_multi_aud, azp_mismatch, nonce_mismatch, auth_time_stale, auth_time_missing, at_hash_missing, at_hash_mismatch, c_hash_missing, c_hash_mismatch, unsupported_alg, alg_required) that each language maps to its own error type. `at_hash`/`c_hash` values are the real OIDC §3.3.2.11 left-half construction — base64url-no-pad of the left-most half of H(value.ascii) where H is the SHA-2 variant of `header_alg` (RS256→SHA-256, ES512→SHA-512, EdDSA→SHA-512); the c_hash for code `Qcb0Orv1...` equals the value in the OIDC Core §3.3.2.11 worked example. Expected outcomes follow the OIDF-certified py-identity-model reference (`core/id_token_logic.py::validate_id_token_claims`). Python (py/src/tests/unit/test_id_token_conformance.py), Go (go/internal/conformance/idtoken_conformance_test.go) and Rust (rust/tests/it/conformance/id_token.rs) each execute every vector of every case and fail if any is skipped. Rule order is the reference order: sub, then a missing aud (IDT-013), then untrusted audiences (§3.1.3.7 step 3), then azp (only with `validate_azp`), nonce, auth_time, at_hash, c_hash. The IDT-003 multiple-audience vectors list their second audience in `trusted_audiences` so they keep exercising the azp rules; without it step 3 rejects them first (IDT-012). The azp rules are opt-in: OIDC Core 1.0 errata set 2 §3.1.3.7 step 4 covers extensions only, step 5 is a MAY/SHOULD, and §2 tells relying parties that use no extensions to ignore azp. With `validate_azp` true, multiple audiences require an azp (`azp_required_multi_aud`, the Core 1.0 (2014) step-4 SHOULD) and a present azp must equal the client_id (`azp_mismatch`, step 5); without it azp is ignored. at_hash/c_hash presence is required per bound value. A supplied access token or code is taken to have come back in the same authorization response as the ID Token (§3.2.2.10, §3.3.2.11: `id_token token`, `code id_token`, `code id_token token`) unless the caller sets its switch (`access_token_issued_with_id_token`/`code_issued_with_id_token`) to false, so by default an absent claim rejects (`at_hash_missing`/`c_hash_missing`). With the switch false — e.g. an ID Token from the token endpoint, where at_hash is OPTIONAL (§3.1.3.6, §3.3.3.6) — an absent claim is accepted and a present one must still match (`*_mismatch`). Absent means the claim key is missing; the presence check runs before the hash is computed, and a switch without its access_token/code has no effect.

tests.title: Valid baseline ID Token
tests.given: A decoded ID Token carrying a non-empty sub and a single audience equal to the client_id
tests.when: The ID-Token profile rules are applied
tests.then: Validation succeeds — sub present, the single audience is the client_id, no optional checks requested

vectors.name: single-string aud equals client_id

tests.title: sub is REQUIRED and must be non-empty
tests.given: A decoded ID Token whose sub claim is absent or empty
tests.when: The ID-Token profile rules are applied
tests.then: Validation is rejected because sub is a required non-empty claim (§2)

vectors.name: sub absent
sub empty string

tests.title: Authorized-party (azp) rules for multiple audiences are opt-in
tests.given: A decoded ID Token whose aud is a single value or a list (every additional audience trusted by the client), with or without azp, and the caller's validate_azp switch
tests.when: The ID-Token profile rules are applied
tests.then: By default azp is ignored (§2). With validate_azp, multiple audiences require an azp (Core 1.0 (2014) §3.1.3.7 step 4 SHOULD, removed in errata set 2) and a present azp must identify this client (errata 2 step 5 MAY/SHOULD)

tests.title: A present azp is compared with the client_id only when azp validation is on
tests.given: A decoded ID Token carrying an azp claim alongside a single audience equal to the client_id, and the caller's validate_azp switch
tests.when: The ID-Token profile rules are applied
tests.then: By default azp is ignored, so a cross-client token (aud is this client, azp is the presenting client) is accepted. With validate_azp, a present azp must equal the client_id (errata 2 §3.1.3.7 step 5)

tests.when: The ID-Token profile rules are applied with the caller nonce set
tests.then: The token nonce MUST be present and equal the caller nonce (§3.1.3.7 step 11)

tests.title: auth_time freshness against max_age
tests.given: A decoded ID Token and a caller max_age (with a fixed now)
tests.when: The ID-Token profile rules are applied with max_age set
tests.then: auth_time MUST be present and satisfy now - auth_time <= max_age + leeway (§3.1.3.7 step 12)

tests.title: at_hash binding under RS256 (SHA-256)
tests.given: A decoded ID Token and an access token, either returned in the same authorization response as the ID Token or not
tests.when: The ID-Token profile rules are applied with the access token set
tests.then: A present at_hash MUST equal the base64url left-half SHA-256 of the access token (§3.3.2.11); an absent at_hash rejects only when the access token was issued with the ID Token (§3.2.2.10, §3.3.2.11), and is accepted otherwise (§3.1.3.6)

tests.title: at_hash binding under ES512 and EdDSA (SHA-512) — algorithm selects the hash
tests.given: A decoded ID Token whose header alg is ES512 or EdDSA and the access token from the same response
tests.when: The ID-Token profile rules are applied with the access token set
tests.then: at_hash MUST equal the base64url left-half SHA-512 of the access token (EdDSA uses SHA-512, as for Ed25519); an SHA-256-sized at_hash under ES512 or EdDSA fails closed (§3.3.2.11)

tests.title: Additional audiences not trusted by the client are rejected
tests.given: A decoded ID Token whose aud carries values other than the client_id, and the caller's list of additional audiences it trusts
tests.when: The ID-Token profile rules are applied
tests.then: Every aud value MUST be the client_id or a trusted audience; any other value rejects the token (§3.1.3.7 step 3). The trusted list only adds trusted values, it cannot switch the check off, and a single audience equal to the client_id is unaffected

tests.title: An ID Token without an audience is rejected
tests.given: A decoded ID Token whose aud is absent, null, an empty string, an empty array, or an array of empty strings
tests.when: The ID-Token profile rules are applied
tests.then: aud is REQUIRED (§2), so a token that names no audience is rejected whether or not a client_id is configured. The check runs after sub and before the untrusted-audience rule
